uncited: HDR-GS initialization and optimization is a method for initializing 3D Gaussian primitives and training a Gaussian Splatting model for High Dynamic Range (HDR) novel view synthesis.

It addresses the limitation of standard 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) which relies on Low Dynamic Range (LDR) images and often lacks accurate Structure-from-Motion (SfM) point clouds for initialization in HDR datasets.

Unlike standard 3DGS which initializes from SfM points of LDR inputs, HDR-GS recalibrates camera parameters using SfM on LDR views captured at a single exposure time to generate initial 3D Gaussian positions, then optimizes the scene using a combined pixel-wise loss and a µ-law domain constraint loss.
This approach establishes a robust data foundation for 3DGS-based algorithms in 3D HDR imaging.
*   A multi-view HDR dataset containing $N_v$ viewpoints.
*   For each viewpoint $j$, LDR images $\hat{I}_{lj}(t_s)$ captured at a specific exposure time $t_s$.
*   Ground truth HDR images $I_{hj}$ (available for synthetic scenes, not for real scenes).
*   Rendered LDR images $\hat{I}_{lj}(\Delta t_j)$ and HDR images $\hat{I}_{hj}$ generated from the current Gaussian set $G$.
*   Recalibrated camera intrinsics $M_{int}$ and extrinsics $\{M_j^{ext}\}_{j=1}^{N_v}$.
*   Initial number of points $N_p$ and their 3D positions $\{\mu_i\}_{i=1}^{N_p}$.
*   Optimized Gaussian parameters (position, features, opacity, scaling, rotation) and tone mapper network weights.
The method initializes the Gaussian set $G$ as described in [GaussianList Data Structure and Initialization](9768-gaussian-list-data-structure-and-initialization.md).
*   **Other Parameters:** Randomly initialized.
Select LDR images $\{\hat{I}_j(t_s)\}_{j=1}^{N_v}$ from the multi-view HDR dataset where all images share the same exposure time $t_s$.
Initialize the Gaussian set $G$ with $N_p$ points at positions $\{\mu_i\}$.
*   **SfM Input Constraint:** Only HDR views under the same exposure time are used as SfM inputs.
*   **Real vs. Synthetic Scenes:** The µ-law constraint loss $L_c$ is not used for real scenes because ground truth HDR images are not provided.
*   **Time Complexity:** Not explicitly given.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Not explicitly given.
It builds on the 3DGS framework [15] and incorporates techniques from HDR-NeRF [14] for handling HDR data.
The method was implemented using PyTorch [75] and tested on datasets collected by [14], including real and synthetic scenes from Blender [74].
